utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, good morning to you. Can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. I can follow the proceedings in my mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, my name is Jan Wubben lead counsel for the Prosecution. Also good morning to my learned friends of the Defence. I'm here together with co-counsel Mr. Gramsci di Fazio and our case manager Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning Your Honours my name is Vasvija Vidovic and together with John Jones I appear for Naser Oric. With us are our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you Madam, and good morning to you and your team. Any preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good morning, Mr. Bekric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. We are going to proceed and conclude with your testimony today. You will be cross-examined starting as from now by Mr. Jan Wubben, who is lead counsel for the Prosecution in this case. Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Wubben:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bektic. My name is, as said, Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. I have some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My first question is: Do you know a place called Bajramovic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever been there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of a meeting in Bajramovici in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you on any meeting with Naser Oric, Atif Ustic, Zulfo Tursunovic and others?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're not aware of a meeting where decisions were made about the command structure of the Srebrenica TO staff?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not -- I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you mentioned the names of Akif Ustic, Zulfo Tursunovic as commanders who had no supreme commander above them.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your basis for that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, like I said yesterday, for Hakija Meholjic is the Sukrija who was our guide from Mocevici area to Srebrenica. He introduced himself as Hakija Meholjic man. And then also from people from my own village who were Hakija Meholjic's unit. And then also people that I know from my village that were in Akif Ustic's unit together with people that I know from Suceska that was of Tursunovic's unit. And from my understanding from talking to people from my closest people that I know from my village there was no supreme command over those commanders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And regarding Zulfo Tursunovic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same thing applies to Zulfo Tursunovic. He did not have a supreme commander and he was not commander of any other commanders in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these people that informed you about that, those facts, did they -- were they present at that meeting, at that meeting in Bajramovic in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I said I'm not aware of the meeting and I do not know if they were present or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about information you had from people related to this topic of command structure. How did that topic arise in your conversation with those people?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The topic in Srebrenica, with the people in Srebrenica, the refugees especially who were in refugee in Srebrenica from Bratunac, that was everyday conversations. You know every single day what's going on the town, who is who, who is the leader, who is the commander, who is in which area. So it's an everyday things you talk about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as such, you're not aware of a meeting in Bajramovici in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I move to the next issue. Yesterday, you stated that you reached Srebrenica in June 1992.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said it was like a ghost town.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was like I said yesterday it was before war very busy, active little town and when we arrived in Srebrenica it was totally deserted, empty, no people. All the cafes, restaurants, stores, everything was empty, looted, glass broken. Many houses burnt, no cars moving around Srebrenica, no people walking around like used to be before war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was pretty quiet, like a ghost town?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was totally it was totally quiet and deserted area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was also the situation in July 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on, as the refugees started flowing in it was getting more and more busy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be specific but you know the group -- first group when we arrived was in June so after that you know the streams of refugees started flowing in. You know, some in smaller groups, some in big groups and continuously -- continually after I arrived and all time I was there, until 1993 the refugees were coming constantly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's by the end of -- starting by the end of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. That's from the time I arrived in Srebrenica, in June, which is the first group of refugees that arrived in Srebrenica. And then after that, continually until April 1993 when I was there, the refugees was streaming in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me go to another issue. Yesterday several attacks or actions had been discussed. You witnessed that thousands of civilians were involved next to fighters.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. That's -- I testified yesterday thousands of refugees who were together with fighters in many actions, some before the fighters, some with the fighters, and many after the fighters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me take the action on Bjelovac as an example. That's December 1992.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So also during the action on Bjelovac, you stated that you were together with thousands of other people from various municipalities.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You and those other civilians, thousands, knew beforehand that this action was going to take place.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew that from the fighters or the family of the fighters involved?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I said yesterday, it is the people from my village, people from the Bratunac municipalities who lived together with their families in their homes and they discussed the actions. And people would talk between each other and basically everybody knew in Srebrenica that actions would take place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So thousands of people, civilians, had to organise to get to the place of the action, the attack.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The refugees were not organised. It's like mobs, going in every single direction. They wanted to go toward the area where the action was taking place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thousands of people had indeed to do a timely start to get to the place of the action, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's definitely true. Some people go the day before, some can go during the night, some can go after. So you can never know with the refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And thousands of people had to make sure as well that they didn't get in the way of the fighters, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not, because many refugees, many civilians were killed and there were in the various actions when the action was taking place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me rephrase my question, then. I'm here in the phase of getting to the place, the route to -- towards the place of the action, not the action itself. So let me rephrase the question. Thousands of people had to make sure that they had to start in time to finally get in time to the place of the action, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about timing part. So many, like I said, refugees who start night before, some would start the same day the action was taking place, some went night before. So it can be -- many came after the action. So many came on time when the action was taking place and many came same day and many came day after and then many other ones came even later, you know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But anyhow, even if this part of it -- I assume that they had to organise to be there and to plan a route, a safe route, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no safe route where refugees went and there was no planning. So with the refugees everybody took their own route whether safe or not safe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they all took the same route?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. Everybody went in different directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they knew where to go from different direction towards the place of the action aforehand?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you go in the action if you have a group, lets say five people or five friends who they want to go to the action they can take their own chances, make their own route, or they can go where there is a route already safe to go there. So it's your chance, it's your life. You take a chance. Do what you want to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then they are all organised together, those thousands of people around the area of the action, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't use the word organised. There were thousands of refugees there but they were not organised, as like I said like animals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I will not compare them with animals but are these civilians, as I may use that qualification, are these civilians there waiting for the action or waiting for any signal?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The refugees who were there when the action is taking place. So they can go during the fighting, after the fighting, whenever they felt like, like I said it's your chance to take to go when there is action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there is of course a resistance to be expected from the inhabitants of the village to be attacked, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there has always been very strong resistance from the inhabitants that live there and from the force that is came from outside into the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And yesterday you used qualifications like fierce fighting, and use of artillery, having heavy weapons. So there should be an element of surprise before such an attack, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you see -- we refugees and the people in Srebrenica were never surprised when we go -- when there is action and when there is shellings and when there is fierce fighting that's nothing new. We knew that Serbs had very strong heavy weapons and they going to use everything at their exposal [sic] to fight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So an element of surprise, attacking by surprise is important for a successful action, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say how it was important you know in the for those people how they planned the action and those people who were in those villages, whether it's important or not. I have no idea. I was not a soldier and I was there as a refugee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- but can I put it to you that if there is no element of surprise, it would be so that the villages attacked will give resistance already by the very appearance of the attackers, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the villagers or the army that was in the villages, they themselves made many actions against the Muslims. So when there is attack against them, they always had weapons and they will confident to defend themselves so I don't think it was a big surprise to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not a real answer to my question, isn't it? So I will ask you again. If there is no element of surprise, it would be so that whenever they are defending their village they will open fire immediately upon appearance of the first attackers they expect.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. They would open fire on the attackers that were being attacked, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this element of surprise is important, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these thousands of people, as you call them refugees, civilians, should also be silent before the attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones? I'm sorry I was looking on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, the last series of questions which I think I have to note, I think is unfair of my learned friend to say that there wasn't a real answer to the question because he's putting a series of speculative questions about would it be important to have surprise if such and such were the case. This witness is not a military expert. He's here testifying about what he saw and experienced and so to put a series of questions about, well, if there were no surprise would this happen; if there were surprise would something else happen; assuming the other would this be important. It's not appropriate for this witness to be asked to have such questions put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the witness is a very intelligent young man and I think he's fully capable of answering only those questions that he can answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. But if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I don't think the questions that are being put are speculative. If he's not in a position to answer them, he's free not to answer them and explain why.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, and in that event if he does give an answer to the best of his ability, I don't think it's fair to say it's not a real answer. He's doing his best to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's not a military expert. I agree with you. He wasn't a military expert then although he knows all the types of weaponry by name and calibre and description.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, from having seen them. It's a different matter altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can understand that at age 14, 13 in those circumstances it's not surprising at all. So when I was much younger than he was then I knew all the fighter jets and bombers and was a keen reader on a daily basis of the Jane's book of aircraft and the Jane's book of -- so. I'm not surprised. Still, it doesn't mean that he's a military expert and we are not considering him as such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, can I also take it that before the action at a certain time, these thousands of civilians, of refugees, around the area of the place of the action, they were silent, they kept silent?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can say where I was, that particular spot, and I can see all thousands around, I know where they were. But you know you know if they kept felt like being silent they would be silent. They were in the hills. Some were silent. Some were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they were indeed silent to such a level that action -- the action would benefit from the surprise element, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really, because when the action is taking place, when you hear firing and shelling in every direction so what's the point in being quiet?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm -- so this is -- this is not an answer to my question. I'm not speaking about when action is taking place. I'm asking you about the phase before the action take place and when -- when those thousands of people were more or less silent to give the fighters the most successful outcome by making use of the element of surprise.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were -- there were -- quiet but they were not I can say silent, absolutely not. Because you can hear children running, screaming. You can hear horses, you can hear everything around. It's not so silent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were close to those thousands of people, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was right there because -- I'm standing right here and 20 metres away I can see somebody is, you know, talking or keeping quiet or, you know, whatever they were doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And place of the action was far away, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first day when I was in Dimnici, the village, it was, you know, not that far. It was -- to Plice upper [phoen] and Pozlodnik, when I was closer to Bjelovac it was much closer than Dimnici but overall it wasn't that far.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the crow flies, probably two, three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So if you make a noise like you described, it won't be heard of on a distance -- at a distance of 2 or 3 kilometres, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you could not hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it safe also to say that everybody thus cooperated in order to achieve a successful action?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. Because where I was, you could not hear when we were -- if I was screaming or yelling. But like I said, there is thousands of refugees all over the place so I can't testify whether refugees down close to Pozlodnik or to -- close to Plice on the first day if they were silent or not, if they were screaming or not, if they were yelling or not, if they were running around or not. I'm testifying where I was. On the first day if I was screaming couldn't hear me. With the other refugees, thousands of them all over the place, I can't testify what they were if they were noisy or they were close to battle or quiet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me move to another issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to have private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session, please. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you testified about an incident during the Kravica attack.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A woman had been slapped because she set a house on fire after she took what she wanted.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. The woman was in the house, took what she wanted, and she set the house on fire and walked the front door and then a fighter slapped her from doing that so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I had not put any question but they will be related so please wait for this information and you will -- you were able to give me an answer. Where in Kravica did that incident occur?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around centre part of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of the day was it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it was mid-morning, sometimes mid -- toward mid-day. So probably I would say mid- to late morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How close were you to that woman?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably ten metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ten metres. So what made you believe that the woman took what she wanted?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I saw what she had in front of her. She had 25 kilos of flour and a bag of full of stuff that she wanted from the house that she carried out side. She had right next to her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell me something about that house? What did the house look like?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was one storey with -- how would I explain to you in -- because basic Bosnian or Balkan house with two -- top -- bottom floor and top floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the woman herself, did you know the name of that woman?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know the woman's name, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever saw her before?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you give her a description of her?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your ability?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. She was probably mid-age, typical, Bosnian woman. I would say she was anywhere between 35, 40 years old who had those Bosnian dress and thing on her head, like a scarf on her head. And she had like everybody else had -- we wear like I said yesterday I wore the sheet but she didn't have the sheet. She had like a top part was white.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was her reaction to the slapping by the fighter?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She screamed back at the fighter and that's about it. Took her stuff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did she scream?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exact same words. It's kind of like -- in kind of way like Go away you idiots, that kind of way. I don't know exactly the wording that she said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your reaction to that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. Looked at it, I kind of felt hate against the fighter and I continue on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you felt hate against the fighter?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can anybody slap the poor woman who came there to get to -- food for her children for herself, for her family, who was expelled from her own place same as I was, and there is this guy who was going to slap her for taking stuff and burn the house?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So she was expelled from the same place as you were. So you knew her?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't mean exact same village I mean probably same as I was, kind of, expelled from the -- from her place, home, wherever was. Same ways I was, probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you felt hate against the fighter. Did you recognise that fighter who slapped her?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I did not recognise him at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the fighter, how he looks like?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had a rifle what we call PAP and he had a kind of like a ragged jacket with sweater and dark pants at the bottom and with the rubber boots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you knew he was a fighter?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's too obvious, if he's got a weapon his shoulder and his hands to me that's fighter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he also wear a kind of ribbon?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no ribbons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No ribbons at all?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No ribbons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not on the held or shoulder?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just average person, like dressed like anybody else would be. The only difference is that he had a gun in his hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the soldier said, this fighter, said anything to you in person?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't with me. I just saw the incident and I continued walking on. He did not say nothing to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw the incident, you were a child, 14 years old, among this action, witnessing a fighter slapping an adult.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this fighter didn't explain to you, a child, this unusual incident?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not the only child there. There was much more -- many people my age, many kids my age, many civilians, women, children, everybody else was there. So the soldier or fighter had nothing to do with me. I just saw the incidents and I continued moving on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will move to another issue. Yesterday you testified about a person --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Wubben. Sorry to interrupt you like this. But you said that this fighter did not have any ribbon, just a rifle, which you also named. How would you have known that he was a Muslim fighter and not a Serbian fighter? How would you have distinguished him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well there is many ways to distinguish, Your Honour. First of all, he was on the same side as civilians who are in the area. If he was a Serbian soldier he would have started shooting everybody around. Secondly, it was very easy to identify between a Serbian soldier and a Muslim soldier. Serbian soldiers got full combat with very sophisticated weapons and then on Muslim side you got a ragged, average man walking around with whatever rifle that can get in their hands with no signs of -- that looked like a soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen the Muslim fighters in any one of the actions that you were present at, wearing headbands or armbands, coloured --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I have not seen that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bekric, yesterday you testified about a person called Hazim Omerovic.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You witnessed that this person made use of resemblance with Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you stated that he'd ask for things, making use of that resemblance.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what would people then give to this Hazim Omerovic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever he would ask for. If he asked for there is bread in the house he asked for that, if there is brandy, he will ask for that, if there is whatever he want, tobacco, he would ask for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall what was the most valuable thing people gave to him?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most valuable thing that they gave to him personally?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what was the most valuable but I'm sure if he -- if he asked for something that people had they would give it to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Give examples of valuable things?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that known of us had very valuable things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bread is valuable, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bread is very valuable. So when you talk about the food that's a different story. Like I said earlier if he asked for bread, they would give him bread. If you ask for tobacco, they would give him tobacco if they had it. If he asked -- they asked for plum brandy, if he would give him plum brandy if they had it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why should people give these valuable things to Hazim Omerovic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say why they gave to him. So obviously they gave it to because they want to give it to him. I can't say why they gave it to him. He acted that way like he thought he introduced himself like he looked like Naser Oric and he acted in the villages -- I'm Naser Oric give me this. So they gave him. Why they gave it to him I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There must be a reason to give this person such things upon the simple request, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure there is reason and if I could find the person that he asked for I would ask him why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you never ask him?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the kind of attention that he liked? Yesterday, you stated that Hazim Omerovic liked the attention; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he -- I'm sure he enjoyed the attention, you know, to act that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah. Was it a kind of joke for Hazim?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a benefit for Hazim. But there was a joke or not, that's -- no idea. I'm sure he benefit from it he has --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or was it indeed just to get favours or both?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No idea. I'm sure he enjoyed the benefit he was getting from it. Was the reason I have no clue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you yourself think it was funny?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it's funny.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm now to the last issue to address in my cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's up to you. I have got a whole day, as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's about PTT building in Srebrenica. Yesterday you stated that your residence in Srebrenica was close to the PTT building.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's about a hundred metres from the house.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that much, yeah, somewhere there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He saw across the road -- a hundred metres across the road from the hospital that's how --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: A kind of triangle, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The hospital was right across from PTT building but my house was a little bit to the left, right next to the hospital, to the left-hand side probably a hundred or so metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw the PTT building a lot of times during your stay in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were even aware of the PTT building before the war, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the function of the PTT building?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war or during the war?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the war.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we knew -- as civilians that there it was a radio communication in PTT building, what we called one address for the all. So all the people that were in Srebrenica during -- in the refuge and they had families outside Srebrenica they would receive messages to that radio communication. Whatever was in PTT I don't know. And then they would post a message saying family -- loved ones writing message from Tuzla or from the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was possible to have contact with the outside world from -- from Srebrenica by means of radio communication?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, like I said, only I know that we received messages from the loved one that were outside Srebrenica. How was in the PTT building, how did they received it, I have no idea whether it was a radio or whatever it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With you the communication was a fact and well known?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I said, I know we received messages but how it was inside I have no idea what kind of communication it was.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Wubben, I would like to know was this so until you had -- was it still like that until you had the incident on the soccer field or was it different at any different -- at any special time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not -- as I can remember, the -- we started receiving messages it was probably late summer and then that I believe went on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Late summer of 1992, in other words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right, late summer 1992. And it was there until Morillon arrived and then after that the peacekeepers were there in the PTT building. So whatever was there after that, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Wubben. I apologise to you for having interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Question: Were you aware of any communication directly to Sarajevo and Tuzla from the PTT building?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: This finalise my cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How would you know? If there was contact with loved ones living outside Srebrenica, how do you exclude the possibility of contacts with Tuzla and Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I am here to testify what I know. So if there was communication, it was. If there wasn't it wasn't. I have no idea if it was or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you didn't say I wouldn't know, I don't know, you said that there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, he said were you aware and he said absolutely not. Absolutely not, he wasn't aware.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When he asked me question if I knew about it I said absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any questions? Judge Brydensholt is going to ask you a question. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: It is only one question. It is regarding this accident or what you would call it where Mr. Bogilovic shot your police cap off your head. Could you give me a little more detail about that. Do you really mean that he shot with a pistol or something your hat off? Or what is it you are telling us?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the centre of the town and I was in the apartment trying to find food and clothing and I found some clothes and I found a police cap which I thought was unique, that I saw before the war. I took it I put it on my head. Walked outside in the street and I saw Becir Bogilovic walking up the street with a rifle in his hand. Just put his rifle on his shoulder aimed it and fired right on my head. Knocked it off my head and it flew far away from me. It flew right off my head, so I don't know how far it went, two metres, five metres, ten metres, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: So he really shot a hole in this hat or cap?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A hole right where the star is on the cap, right above it. Like, right there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How far was he from you when he shot, when he fired the rifle?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anywhere between ten, 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Mr. Bekric, I also have some questions. Yesterday you have been asked with regard to your knowledge of Naser Oric, and you told us that you did not see him between beginning of the war and the arrival of Morillon. Now, you had seen him before the war, on what occasion? How did you got to know him? How did you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I said yesterday that I knew Naser from before war from my village. He came in my village. In the village you know everybody that lives in it and comes in it and goes through it. So Naser comes in the village or whatever so before the war I knew who he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: That was Voljevica.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And do you know where Naser Oric is born?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, Naser Oric is from the Potocari area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: This is normal, that people move around in those villages?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was before war, it was normal to move around villages, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you did not see him between the beginning of the war and the arrival of General Morillon. But did you hear of him, if you did not see him? Perhaps you may have heard of him.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I heard from people talking that people from Potocari with Naser having a fierce attacks coming from Bratunac and they are fighting the front line in Potocari, resisting the breakthrough from Zvijezda and from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: What do you mean with fierce attack? Was he leading a group or --

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the beginning of the war, the -- when the paramilitary -- Arkan's paramilitary came from Bratunac area so that's where people from Potocari stood up to them and then that's where they had front line and that's where there was more vulnerable attacks from Bratunac area and from Zvijezda and/or from the hills around from Caus, shelling was coming towards Potocari. And it was a very main key to Srebrenica to -- for survival of Srebrenica at the breakthrough from Bratunac through Potocari. Then whole Srebrenica would be in crisis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And this incident you talked about, was it the only one where you according to your knowledge, Naser Oric was involved?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, people admired Naser Oric because he stood up in beginning of war with the people from Potocari to Arkan's men and that's -- the people from Srebrenica and people from Bratunac knew that Naser's -- Naser and people from Potocari were located in Potocari area all through the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: So he was only involved in the fight against Arkan?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was involved with the -- anybody who attacked Potocari area from all different directions, from Bratunac, from Zvijezda, from Caus from all different directions. From Glogova area, that part. So whoever attacked that area they were involved defending the Potocari area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Can I conclude from your answer that Naser Oric at least was a leader of a group fighting against certain Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I'm saying, from talking to people in Srebrenica, that Naser together with the other men in Potocari were holding front lines that were coming to Bratunac. Whether he was commander at Potocari area, whether he was an average man as everybody else I have no clue, I can't testify to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: If he was a normal fighter as anybody else was, why was it so important to -- for instance for Hazim to be confused with him that people would be impressed if they say, I am Naser Oric? I mean, if he was only a normal soldier, what is impressive of that, when you have thousands of people of this sort.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, Hazim imitated Naser Oric but there was many other men who imitated other leaders and other men who were admired. To me and to other people that I know, Naser is admired as much as any other leaders in Srebrenica who were -- who stood up to Serbian aggression. So it was not specially Naser Oric. There was many people who liked Naser Oric. There was many people who liked Zulfo Tursunovic as much as Naser Oric. This and there were people who admired Hakija Meholjic more than admired Naser Oric. So it's not like just Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: You told us that you have arrived rather close to Hakija, that you knew him, that you also knew Zulfo who has been a relative of your father, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Distant relative of my father.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: At any rate, you know Zulfo, you know Hakija. Did you ever hear of any incidents that somebody would say, "I am Hakija, I am Zulfo, please give me this or that"? Did you hear any -- at any time hear of such a thing?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see personally say Give me this, Give me that but I see many people in Srebrenica imitate leaders like Zulfo the way he was, Hakija Meholjic the way he was, the way Nedzad Bektic was. Many people imitated them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: It was very easy to go around and tell I am this or that man and you got whatever you wanted.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last part of the question I did not understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: So it was very easy in Srebrenica according to what you know, what you know, that you could just go around and walk around Srebrenica and say, I am Hakija, I am Zulfo, I am this or that and you got what you wanted. Is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In Srebrenica the way it was in Srebrenica everybody did what they wanted, how they wanted, when they wanted. It was no law, it was no -- nothing to prevent, say, don't do this or don't do that. So everybody acted the way they wanted. They dressed the clothes the way they wanted, imitated by what they wanted did what they liked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And did you personally ever attend -- have been present when somebody would -- when Hazim would introduce himself as Naser Oric? Have you ever been present at such an occasion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was present in Konjevic Polje and Suceska when he introduced himself that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And you knew it was not Naser Oric who but Hazim who presented himself as Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And you did not explain to the people that they have mistakenly given something to a man who was in reality not Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The more you keep quiet the better you off. So everybody did their own business, what they wanted. I kept my own business to myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have one question arising out of the last question that Judge Eser. You said you heard this Hazim present himself as Naser Oric and ask for things when you were in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: M'hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If Naser Oric was based in Potocari the way you have described things, he had nothing else to do with the rest of the territory, why on earth would Hazim Omerovic try to obtain whatever, pretending to be Naser Oric in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I cannot answer that. I have no idea why he acted that way. I'm sure Hazim knew Naser possibly before the war or they met somewhere but I can't testify why he acted that way in Konjevic Polje or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. In Kravica, when you were in Kravica during the action in Kravica, did you see Naser Oric there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I have not seen Naser Oric there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you ever see Naser Oric in any of -- present in any of the actions that you were present for?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. Like I said, I only -- the only time I saw Naser was before war and in the PTT building when Morillon came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you ever see him on a horse?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not seen him on a horse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. That brings --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just ask two questions in light of the questions which Your Honours have asked, just two brief questions of re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You were asked about this phenomenon, if you like, of people imitating Nedzad Bektic, Zulfo Tursunovic and others. At this time were there television images or magazines or newspapers which carried pictures of these people so that people who -- knew who they were?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Srebrenica there was no magazines, there was no newspapers to carry the pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And the second question: Were you when you spoke of Naser Oric being in Potocari, were you testifying that he remained in Potocari throughout the whole time and never left Potocari once, or are you testifying that you don't know -- you don't know of his movements over the whole period?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From talking to people he was in Potocari. Now whether he moved around or not, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bekric, I must thank you for having come over in spite of everything and give testimony in this case. If it's difficult for other persons, it's more difficult for you. I can quite understand. So please do accept our sense of appreciation, Judge Brydensholt, Judge Eser and myself and our gratitude for your having come over to give testimony in this case. Madam Usher, now as soon as we are all gone, will assist you, together with the rest of the staff, to enable you to return back to your hotel, and then you will receive all the further assistance that you require to facilitate your return back home from where you came from. My last message to you is on behalf of everyone present here and that is to wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jones, before we leave, it's okay. I know that the sitting ends here and we will not be sitting at 1.00. However I wanted you to know that I had every intention to ask everyone here to observe a two minute silence at 1.00 in remembrance of the events, the unfortunate events, that took place in London last week. Please I want you to know that we will be observing two minutes silence in our respective chambers.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's very kind. I appreciate that, Your Honour.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.00 a.m.
